w: Bergen's easiest mountain view: the Floibanen funicular hauls you from the harbourfront to 320 metres in about eight minutes flat, no hiking boots required. The name may come from an old weather vane that once told sailing ships which way the wind blew - useful information for a city built entirely on shipping.
s: An eight-minute funicular ride to Bergen's best view
_facts: One of the 'seven city mountains' surrounding central Bergen, highest point 400 metres
Name possibly derives from a weather vane (floystangen) once used to show wind direction for sailing ships
The Floibanen funicular takes passengers from the city centre to 320 metres in about eight minutes
A popular viewpoint over the Bergen peninsula for tourists and locals alike

w: Edvard Grieg composed some of Norway's most famous music in a tiny wooden hut on this property, steps from the villa he shared with his wife Nina - and steps from the spot where they are both buried. The whole site is preserved as a museum now: hut, villa, gravesite and all, exactly where he left it.
s: Grieg's home, composing hut and grave, all in one place
_facts: Former home of composer Edvard Grieg and his wife Nina Grieg, in Bergen
Site includes the Edvard Grieg Museum, Grieg's villa, the hut where he composed music, and the couple's gravesite

w: A proper cabinet-of-curiosities museum run by the university - anthropology next to archaeology, geology next to zoology, art next to cultural history, all under one academic roof. The kind of place where wandering off-topic for an hour is basically the intended experience.
s: A university museum spanning bones, rocks and art alike
_facts: University museum in Bergen covering anthropology, archaeology, botany, geology, zoology, art and cultural history

w: Norway's first prime minister after independence from Sweden, Christian Michelsen, built this as his home and lived out his life here - his friends then raised the money to buy it for the nation when he died in 1925. The park opened to the public that year, and it's been the royal family's Bergen residence since 1927.
s: The shipping magnate PM's home, now a royal residence
_facts: Royal castle in Bergen with a history reaching back to the Middle Ages, owned in turn by some of the city's wealthiest men
Current main building commissioned by Christian Michelsen, shipping magnate and Norway's first prime minister after the 1905 dissolution of the union with Sweden
After Michelsen's death in 1925, friends and colleagues raised funds so the state could buy the property; the park opened to the public that year
The Norwegian royal family's residence in Bergen since 1927

w: The tallest of Bergen's seven surrounding peaks at 643 metres, Ulriken has a cable car straight to the summit for anyone who'd rather skip the climb, and a genuine trail network for anyone who wouldn't. A TV tower, a restaurant, and a view over the whole fjord-cut city wait at the top either way.
s: Bergen's highest peak, by cable car or by foot
_facts: Highest of the Seven Mountains surrounding Bergen, at 643 metres
Served by the Ulriksbanen aerial tramway to the summit, where there is a TV tower and a restaurant
A network of trails offers hikes ranging from steep to easy

w: Guarding the mouth of Bergen harbour since medieval times, Bergenhus is one of the oldest and best-preserved stone fortifications left standing in all of Norway. Every ship that ever sailed into the Hanseatic city's port sailed past these walls first - the gatekeeper of Bergen's whole trading history.
s: One of Norway's oldest stone forts, guarding the harbour
_facts: Fortress located at the entrance to Bergen harbour
One of the oldest and best-preserved stone fortifications in Norway

w: Construction started in the 1130s and finished around 1180, which makes this the oldest building still standing anywhere in Bergen - older than the Bryggen wharves it looks out over. Fire has come for it more than once since, most recently patched up in 2013, but the grey stone bones underneath are the real thing.
s: Bergen's oldest surviving building, since around 1180
_facts: Parish church of the Church of Norway, located in the Bryggen area of Bergen
Construction believed to have started in the 1130s or 1140s and completed around 1180
The oldest remaining building in the whole city of Bergen
Damaged by fires over the centuries, with renovations most recently in 2013

w: There isn't much on record beyond the name and the address, but the name alone tells you what you're getting: a museum dedicated to the Hanseatic merchants who once ran Bergen's trade from this stretch of the harbour. Sometimes the shortest catalogue entry points at the biggest story.
s: A museum built on the name of Bergen's Hanseatic past
_facts: Museum in the city of Bergen, Norway
